       The best sorting network currently known for 256 elements, due to D. Van
  Voorhis, shows that S^(256)  3651, compared to 3839 by Batcher's method.
  [See R. L. Drysdale and F. H. Young, SICOMP 4 (1975), 264{270.] As n ! 1,
  it turns out in fact that S^(n) = O(n log n); this astonishing upper bound was
  proved by Ajtai, Komlos, and Szemeredi, Combinatorica 3 (1983), 1{19. The
  networks they constructed are not of practical interest, since they use many
  comparators just to save a factor of log n. Batcher's method is much better,
  unless n exceeds the total memory capacity of all computers on earth! But their
  theorem establishes the true asymptotic growth of S^(n), up to a constant factor.
